You are working in freytag-forge (Python 3.12). Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp; run `.venv/bin/python` (never uv). Run tests with `env -u CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL -u CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_TOKEN .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov <files>`. No network, no live model call. Do not git commit. NEVER print or write any credential. NO regular expressions in new code. No story vocabulary (no Kristin, truck, laptop, drawer, Michelle) in non-test code. Tests may use the shipped continuity-initiative package through the helpers in tests/test_observation_mode.py (`_state_at`) and tests/test_observation_shadow.py, plus a synthetic second story. Write the tests FIRST, run them and confirm they fail for the right reason, then implement until they pass. Do not edit any file outside YOU MAY EDIT ONLY. Run ruff check and ruff format on your files at the end. BACKGROUND. RuntimeEngine._turn_active (storygame/runtime/engine.py) loops up to TURN_NARRATION_ATTEMPTS=2 times: provider call, reveal resolve, validate_effects, a deepcopy `candidate_state` with `apply_proposal(proposal, apply_world=False)`, then narration_validator.validate; a ProposalValidationError on the first attempt triggers one retry with provider.note_rejection(code). Only AFTER the loop does it call state.apply_proposal(proposal) and then WorldCapture.after_commit(command, narration, entered_scene=...), which calls ItemFactsProvider.apply_item_facts(raw, ...) and that MUTATES state.facts (World over state.facts), provider fields and makes billed model calls: one item-facts match call via CloudflareTurnProvider._request_item_facts and Jev mapping checks through the `confirm` lambda. Observation context: ItemFactsProvider._observation_context() and storygame/runtime/observation_verifier.py (ObservationVerifier, relations_from_context, fail-closed verdicts; `report.accepted` is True only when outcome is 'ok' and every verdict is 'accept'). The verifier is already built and must not change. YOU MAY EDIT ONLY: storygame/runtime/observation_preview.py, storygame/runtime/capture.py, storygame/runtime/engine.py, tests/test_observation_resume.py (NEW), and tests/test_observation_enforcement.py (only to adjust tests that this task legitimately changes; say which). 

CONTEXT. T8a/T8a2/T8b are done: read observation_preview.py, WorldCapture.preview_commit/take_preview/after_commit/context/resume in capture.py, RuntimeEngine._preview_observation, the changes in _turn_active, and resolve_break in engine.py, plus tests/test_observation_preview.py and tests/test_observation_enforcement.py. Enforcement is OFF in the product (`WorldCapture.enforcing_verifier` is None), and the default product path must stay behaviorally identical. 

BUILD. (1) GATE T8b's engine additions on enforcement. T8b made every turn call `self.capture.context()` and deep-copy provider fields (pre_turn_context / pre_turn_provider_fields), and made the NarrationProviderError branch call `capture.discard()` and `capture.resume(...)` even when enforcement is off. Gate all of that on `self.capture is not None and self.capture.enforcing_verifier is not None` (a small helper such as `_enforcing()` is fine) so with enforcement off the engine does exactly what it did before T8 (no context() call, no extra discard/resume). Add a test that, with enforcement off, `capture.context` is not called during a turn and a NarrationProviderError leaves the provider exactly as the pre-T8 code did (compare against calling the same sequence with the T8 gate bypassed is not needed: assert context/discard/resume spies were not called). (2) PREVIEW FAILURE IS FAIL CLOSED. In `_preview_observation`, an unexpected Exception from `preview_commit` that is NOT a NarrationProviderError (and not a ProposalValidationError) must become `ProposalValidationError('The observation check could not complete.', code='observation_preview_failed')` (raised `from error`), so it takes the same retry/reject/rollback path, and `capture.resume(pre_turn_context)` also runs for that code. NarrationProviderError keeps its existing operational-failure path. (3) GAME-BREAK RESUME. `WorldCapture.context()` must include the pending preview when `_pending_preview` is not None (key 'observation_preview': a JSON-compatible dict built by new `CandidatePreview.to_json()`), and must NOT add the key when there is none (so existing contexts are byte-identical). `CandidatePreview.from_json(data)` rebuilds it, including `CallMemo.from_json`. `WorldCapture.resume(context)` restores `_pending_preview` from the key, or sets it to None when the key is absent. `CandidatePreview.facts_after` and every field must survive a JSON round trip (json.dumps/loads) unchanged; tuples may come back as lists but comparisons in `after_commit` (`observation_diverged`) must still be correct, so normalize in from_json. In `resolve_break('proceed')`, `self.capture.resume(pending_capture)` then `after_commit(command, pending.narration, ...)` must therefore consume the preview and replay the billed answers (no live match or confirm call). (4) DIVERGENCE ON PROCEED. In `RuntimeEngine.resolve_break`, take `pending_snapshot = self.state.pending_snapshot` before `self.state.resolve_break(decision)`. After `after_commit` in the proceed path, if `capture_record.get('observation_diverged')` is true: `self.capture.discard()`, `self.state.restore_snapshot(pending_snapshot)`, `self._clear_provider_handoff()` and raise `ProposalValidationError('The committed effects differ from the previewed effects.', code='observation_diverged')` so nothing from the proceeded turn remains and the player can re-enter the command. Document in a comment that provider turn-output fields are reset by the next turn's before_turn. 

TESTS FIRST in tests/test_observation_resume.py (hermetic; reuse the fixtures of tests/test_observation_enforcement.py and tests/test_runtime_capture.py game-break tests around lines 155-165 and 319): a context() has no 'observation_preview' key without a preview, and the whole context equals today's (compare to a copy taken with no verifier). b preview -> context() -> json round trip -> a FRESH capture/provider .resume() -> after_commit consumes the memo: zero live match calls and zero live confirm calls, committed world equals the uncommitted-path result, observation_diverged False. c at-risk game break (future dependency) with enforcement on: the turn returns a game_break, `state.pending_capture` is JSON-serializable (json.dumps works), the whole RuntimeState survives model_dump_json / model_validate_json, and `engine.resolve_break('proceed')` on the restored state commits exactly once with zero extra billed calls, correct item facts, single pacing and single seating; `resolve_break('return_to_scene')` restores the pre-turn snapshot exactly and leaves no pending preview. d post-commit game break (the 'newly unsatisfied' branch after after_commit) with enforcement on: same proceed/return checks. e divergence on proceed (tamper with the restored state before proceeding) -> ProposalValidationError code 'observation_diverged', facts equal the pending snapshot's, no pending break, the next turn runs normally. f FAULT INJECTION: parametrize a fault at each of these points and prove EXACT rollback (state.snapshot() equals the pre-turn snapshot; the generic vars(provider) snapshot excluding billing counters equals the pre-turn one; no segments; attempt recorded) and that the narration provider is called at most 2 times and item-facts match calls at most 2: preview_commit raises RuntimeError on attempt 1 (then succeeds on 2 -> committed once) and on both attempts (rejected, code 'observation_preview_failed'); verifier raises; verifier returns None; the `ask` used for Jev confirm raises inside the preview; after_commit raises inside the real application. Where an unexpected exception from after_commit cannot be made fail closed without widening scope, assert only what the existing engine does and say so in your report. g a verdict from attempt 1 is never consumed by attempt 2 (stale preview dropped). h a synthetic second story passes b and f. 

FINISH: run the check's suites, ruff check and format; report counts, list the test_observation_enforcement.py edits, and quote the resume/context code.
